narrative.documentConcept: PD autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, constipation, bladder
narrative.text: This section covers Parkinson’s autonomic symptoms: orthostatic hypotension, constipation and bladder symptoms. OH management combines medication review and nonpharmacological measures with selected drugs while monitoring supine hypertension. Constipation can involve slow transit and impaired evacuation; macrogol and lubiprostone have trial support. The cited review describes bladder assessment as checking coexisting urological disease and medication trade-offs. Antimuscarinics may worsen constipation, while mirabegron trials have differing outcomes. Probiotic recommendations also differ across evidence reviews; product-specific and short-term results should retain their qualifications.

narrative.documentConcept: PD autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, constipation, bladder
narrative.text: The 2019 MDS review called probiotics with prebiotic fiber efficacious and clinically useful on the basis of one trial; the 2022 meta-analysis instead concluded that evidence remained insufficient, noting few trials, heterogeneous preparations and high heterogeneity. These are attributed assessments with different evidence sets, not an unconditional endorsement of probiotics.

narrative.documentConcept: PD autonomic dysfunction: orthostatic hypotension, constipation, bladder
narrative.text: Mirabegron bladder-trial findings differ: PaDoMi reported improved OAB symptom scores and another placebo-controlled PD trial reported positive primary outcomes, whereas MAESTRO found no significant primary composite-score benefit from adding mirabegron to behavioral modification. Results should be interpreted by population, comparator and endpoint.

narrative.documentConcept: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
narrative.text: PD cognitive treatment depends on whether functional independence is preserved or cognition impairs daily activities. Rivastigmine has the strongest established drug evidence for PD dementia, with moderate benefits and tolerability trade-offs. Dementia drug results should not be generalized to PD-MCI. Cognitive training, stimulation and aerobic activity have different roles and evidence limits; durable prevention of cognitive decline remains unproven. Guideline recommendations for memantine and galantamine differ and require attribution to the issuing guideline and date.

narrative.documentConcept: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
narrative.text: Memantine recommendations differ: NICE NG71 (2017) allows consideration only when cholinesterase inhibitors are contraindicated or not tolerated, whereas the 2024 German guideline recommends against memantine for PD dementia.

narrative.documentConcept: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
narrative.text: Galantamine recommendations also differ by guideline and date: the 2019 MDS review calls it possibly useful despite insufficient PD dementia efficacy evidence; the 2024 German guideline recommends against its use.

narrative.documentConcept: PD cognitive impairment and dementia treatment
narrative.text: Cognitive training has mixed evidence: the German guideline supports it for PD-MCI but notes small, heterogeneous trials; an eight-week computerized-training RCT in PD patients with subjective cognitive complaints found no benefit on primary planning accuracy and no group differences at follow-up. The populations and interventions differ, so this is a limitation on generalization rather than proof that every training program fails.

narrative.documentConcept: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
narrative.text: The cited sources describe specialist assessment and targeted treatment for PD swallowing, saliva and communication problems. Swallowing impairment can cause aspiration pneumonia and nutritional harm; instrumental assessment guides management. EMST has short-term swallowing trial evidence, but comparative and long-term dysphagia treatment evidence remains limited. Botulinum toxin has randomized evidence for drooling, with dry mouth and dysphagia reported as adverse events. LSVT LOUD improved participant-reported voice handicap in PD COMM, although vocal strain and trial design limit interpretation. Speech and language therapy also addresses communication strategies and changing equipment needs.

narrative.documentConcept: PD dysphagia, sialorrhea, speech and voice problems
narrative.text: Troche’s positive EMST swallowing-safety result coexists with Gandhi and Steele’s cautious systematic-review conclusion that lower-risk-of-bias studies supported efficiency rather than safety benefits; this is an evidence-certainty difference, not proof the trial result is false.

narrative.documentConcept: PD neuropsychiatric symptoms: psychosis, depression, anxiety, apathy
narrative.text: The cited sources treat PD psychosis, depression, anxiety and apathy as distinct problems with distinct assessment and treatment choices. Psychosis care includes checking medical and medication triggers; clozapine and pimavanserin have stronger efficacy evidence than quetiapine. Depression has antidepressant and CBT trial evidence. Anxiety CBT results depend partly on the outcome scale. Apathy can occur independently of depression, and treatment findings from small or selected populations need careful qualification. These distinctions matter because apparent benefit in one syndrome or short trial does not establish benefit or long-term safety across all four.

narrative.documentConcept: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms
narrative.text: Pain, fatigue and sensory disturbances contribute to disability in Parkinson’s disease. The cited sources characterize pain by syndrome; sensory symptoms can involve peripheral neuropathy as well as altered perception. Fatigue is distinct from sleepiness; Parkinson’s Foundation guidance describes assessing other causes, pacing activity and regular exercise. Treatment evidence is uneven: historical MDS ratings are qualified, PANDA and OXYDOPA did not establish their primary analgesic benefits, and sham-controlled acupuncture studies did not show a fatigue-specific advantage. Laboratory changes in pain thresholds should not be equated with durable clinical pain relief. Preliminary stimulation studies remain specific to the pain types and follow-up studied.

narrative.documentConcept: PD pain, fatigue and sensory symptoms
narrative.text: Experimental findings on sensory thresholds conflict: one study reported that thermal and mechanical pain thresholds were uninfluenced by levodopa or STN-DBS, whereas another reported significant increases in mechanical pain and tolerance thresholds after acute STN-DBS and after acute levodopa administration. A uniform direct effect on central pain processing is not established by these studies.

narrative.documentConcept: PD sleep disorders: RBD, insomnia and daytime sleepiness
narrative.text: The cited sources distinguish dream enactment with injury risk, insomnia, and daytime sleepiness in PD. The AASM guideline pairs environmental safety advice with conditional drug options for RBD; clonazepam and immediate-release melatonin have conditional guideline support, while prolonged-release melatonin failed in a small PD trial. Insomnia assessment considers other sleep disorders, and CBT-I evidence in PD is promising but limited by small studies and adherence. NICE describes a medication review, a search for reversible causes and driving precautions for daytime sleepiness. Modafinil has mixed efficacy evidence; CPAP evidence applies to coexisting obstructive sleep apnea. Guideline options and positive pooled findings should retain their evidence limitations.
